output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) reported dispute tickets roughly doubled since August and requested an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01). An initial problem framing (PD-1@v1) attributed the surge mainly to a billing-side defect on ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025, E-03), ruling out tariff change (E-02) and field read-collection failure (E-01). New AMI read-event evidence (E-12) invalidated that framing: 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes actually had valid, before-cutoff AMI reads that billing import wrongly rejected as HIGH_CONSUMPTION. The problem was redefined (PD-1@v2, DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS) around a confirmed root cause: billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), compares raw register values directly against 12-month m3 history; firmware v4.2 meters rolled out 2026-06 report in 0.1 m3 units versus v3.x meters' m3 units (E-14), so v4.2 readings appear ~10x true consumption, triggering false HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections and forced estimate substitution (hypotheses H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT and H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT, both CONFIRMED). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the agent delivered a read-only analysis report of the BV-17/firmware defect (DA-RULES) and a dispute-volume trend report (DA-TICKET), per solution design SD-2's release scope, with no automated bill or dispatch writes, consistent with constraints K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH. The actual rule fix and any re-billing of affected accounts were not deployed; they require Billing Operations (SH-BILL) action outside this agent/harness and could not be verified as deployed within contest time.
key_points: Root problem established via evidence chain: dispute volume doubled (E-07: 610→590→1180→1260 tickets Jun-Sep); tariff change ruled out (E-02); AMI read-event data (E-12) showed 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-dispute accounts had valid pre-cutoff reads wrongly rejected as HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not missing reads.

Mechanism confirmed by linking billing-config rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-13) with meter firmware data showing v4.2 meters report in 0.1 m3 while v3.x report in m3 (E-14), producing a ~10x apparent consumption spike.

An earlier evidence revision (ER-1, ER-2) corrected the interpretation of E-01 and E-03: the field-staffing/route-completion shortfall and the ACTUAL-vs-ESTIMATED read split do not establish field-collection failure as the dominant cause; this invalidated the prior problem definition PD-1@v1 and its dependent solution design, remedies, and work items per dependency review DR-1.

Release scope (SD-2) was limited to read-only analysis/reporting work items (analyze_billing_validation_rule_changes:DA-RULES, monitor_dispute_volume_trend:DA-TICKET); no write_bill_adjustment or push_route_update actions were taken, matching constraints K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

Why majority of disputed bills carry ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads (1785 of 3025, E-03) is NOT yet explained by the confirmed BV-17 mechanism; this is tracked as VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM, left OPEN and outside release scope.

Structural remedies to actually fix the defect (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX: correct unit conversion in BV-17; SR-REBILL-AFFECTED-ESTIMATED-AC: re-bill the 1184 affected accounts) were identified but not deployed in this release — they require Billing Operations (SH-BILL) action outside the agent/harness surface and could not be verified within contest time.
The DEFINE Gate result for the current problem definition was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release.
limitations_explained: A semantic check (semantic:data_completeness_claim_consistency) failed: the release's own stated limitation text claims DA-RULES/DA-TICKET completeness is UNKNOWN, but the data_assets catalog actually records both as COMPLETE — this is an internal inconsistency in the release notes that the Human should be aware of.

VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM is OPEN: the specific cause of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills is unresolved and was excluded from this release's scope, so the ACTUAL-read portion of the dispute surge remains unexplained.

VOB-R-3 is OPEN (required before production use): it has not been established whether monthly dispute ticket volume (E-07, M-DISPUTE-VOL) is a valid sole proxy for 'bills are correct,' since it may include disputes unrelated to the confirmed billing defects.

The rule fix itself (correcting BV-17's unit conversion) and any re-billing of the 1184 wrongly-rejected accounts remain unfinished; they require Billing Operations action outside this agent/harness and were not verified as deployed.

DA-RULES completeness relies on assumption A-RULE-LOG-COMPLETE (status ACTIVE, unproven) that the billing-config rule-change log captured all relevant changes, so undetected rule changes beyond BV-17/BV-09 could exist and go unflagged.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY is OPEN: dispute ticket volume may include contact drivers unrelated to the identified billing defects, limiting confidence in it as the sole measure that bills are now correct.
The DEFINE Gate for the current problem passed only CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some review findings and deferred items were tracked as VOBs rather than fully cleared before this release.
